subject: Subprocessor retention & backup custody — alignment and remediation checklist
messages:
From: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@medbridge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@medbridge.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor retention & backup custody — initial ask

Hi Naomi,

Quick note from Legal / Ops at MedBridge. As part of our intake we need a short playbook describing:
- how Redwood handles backup purges (timeline from deletion request -> snapshot deletion),
- how subprocessors are notified and their retention windows coordinated,
- what evidence we can get for a customer-initiated erase (logs, escrow snapshots, attestations).

Specific asks:
1) Can you provide the max timeframe between a customer deletion request and the actual removal from backups (worst-case across regions)?
2) Are there any exceptions for log / KV caches that may persist beyond snapshot deletion? If so, what are the remediation controls?
3) Do you have a template runbook we can reference for a coordinated erase that includes subprocessor handoff and escrow steps?

We need this for our SOC2 readiness review next month. If you have an S3/object purge matrix or a short checklist we can attach to our evidence pack, that would be perfect.

Thanks — happy to sync if a quick call is easier.

— Samuel
Samuel Ortiz
Director, Security & Compliance
MedBridge

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Ortiz <samuel.ortiz@medbridge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor retention & backup custody — initial ask

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise playbook and an S3/escrow matrix (see attachments) that maps triggers -> actions -> owners. High-level answers up front:

1) Worst-case backup purge timing: 90 days from deletion request for geo-distributed cold snapshots in our Dedicated/Private paths. Typical hosted path is 30 days but depends on snapshot rotation schedule and region (we include per-region exceptions in the matrix).

2) Logs / KV caches: short-term ephemeral caches (KV cache used for inference) are purged on a ~24–72 hour cadence in hosted; however, operational logs (telemetry, tracing) have separate retention and may require a formal erase request for evidence. We include a remediation flow: rekey & tombstone -> purge index -> verify checksums -> attestation.

3) Runbook: included as a one-page checklist — steps for customer request intake, legal hold check, subprocessor notification, escrow snapshot expiry, and evidence bundle generation.

See attachments: [attachment: S3_escrow_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 43KB)], [attachment: dpa_redline_v2.pdf (pdf, 98KB)].

Next steps I propose: 1) Ops (Jonas) to confirm regional purge timing in the matrix; 2) Infra (Karthik) to confirm KV/log purge cadence and propose a short remediation attestation we can provide to customers; 3) Legal (Kim) to suggest language we can add to the DPA about escrow/custody evidence.

If that sounds good I can produce a 1-page artifact you can include in the SOC2 evidence pack. Happy to jump on a 20m call if you prefer.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Privacy, Redwood Inference

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 11:02 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sam — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise playbook and an S3/escrow matrix (see attachments) that maps triggers -> actions -> owners.

Quick technical notes from infra:
- Hosted (multi-tenant) snapshots: rotation window is configurable per-customer; default retention for long-term snapshots is 30 days. Backups in cold region tier may remain until next scheduled snapshot compaction — worst-case we treat as 90 days for evidence planning.
- Dedicated / Private: customers can set snapshot retention via console; for customers on reserved capacity we often agree to 45–90 day escrow windows as part of procurement.
- KV cache and prefix caches: these are eviction-based and for safety we consider them "ephemeral" (24–72 hours). However, telemetry/logging pipelines ingest copies to our analytics cluster — those copies have 180-day retention by default unless a retention carveout is applied.

Remediation controls we can offer:
1) Immediate tombstone + rekey for customer keys (when requested).
2) Targeted snapshot invalidation + expedited compaction (operational run, 24–72 hours to complete).
3) For telemetry, we can provide an evidence package containing: purge runbook output, hash attestations for deleted snapshots, and a timeline of subprocessor notifications.

I'll validate the exact region-level worst-case numbers and update the S3_escrow_matrix. For now I recommend we present conservative numbers to MedBridge and offer an SLA exception window in writing if they need a faster purge path.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Thanks all — forwarding a short DPA language suggestion and a proposed evidence checklist. Key asks from Legal side:
- Add an escrow clause that specifies the maximum backup purge window (we propose "no greater than 90 days for cold-region snapshots unless otherwise agreed").
- Include a clause describing log carveouts and the process for an expedited telemetry purge (customer must supply written erase request + authorized contact).
- Define what constitutes acceptable evidence: attestation signed by Redwood Security, purge log export, and snapshot hash list.

I'll upload a redline to the DPA and route via DocuSign once we agree on the wording. For the SOC2 pack: Naomi, can you produce the 1-page artifact you mentioned that ties the matrix, the runbook checklist, and the attestation template together? I'll make a legal-friendly cover note.

Sam — if you can confirm MedBridge's required maximum purge window (and whether you want an SLA exception path), we will include that in the redline.
